title: Readable patterns: options objects and named parameters
hook: JavaScript has no overloading — the options object pattern plus destructured defaults is how libraries express named parameters without ten-argument function signatures.

blocks.text: **Options object pattern**: single parameter `{ host, port, timeout }` with defaults via destructuring. Improves readability vs positional args (what was `true, false, 3`?). **Named parameters** simulated through object keys — order-independent. Combines with **spread** for layering defaults. TypeScript types it as **interface Options** or **Partial<T>**. Node APIs migrated from `(a, b, cb)` to `{ ...opts }` style over time.

entries.plainDefinition: Single config object argument instead of many positional parameters.
Required keys validated in factory; optional get defaults in destructure.
TypeScript utility making all properties optional for override objects.
Named keys self-document in IDE autocomplete vs positional order.
entries.example: VS Code hints property names on fetch second arg.

blocks.text: Public SDKs (AWS SDK v3, fetch, Prisma) use options objects for forward-compatible evolution — add fields without breaking callers. Positional APIs break when you insert a new middle parameter. C# uses **optional parameters** and **named arguments** at call site: `Connect(host: "x", port: 443)` — similar ergonomics, different mechanism.

blocks.title: Interview trap: empty call
blocks.body: function f({ a = 1 } = {}) allows f() with no args. Without = {} on parameter, f() throws destructuring undefined.

snippet.label: Options object with defaults
snippet.explanation: Frozen DEFAULTS prevent mutation leak; spread merge; destructure for implementation.

snippet.label: Destructured parameter style
snippet.explanation: Named params at call site — order free. = {} allows empty paginate().

snippet.label: C# named arguments
snippet.code:
Connect(host: "db.internal", port: 5432, ssl: true);

public void Connect(string host, int port = 5432, bool ssl = false) { }
snippet.explanation: C# optional + named args at call site — JS achieves similar via options object.

snippet.label: Failure mode: mutable shared DEFAULTS
snippet.explanation: Clone nested defaults per instance or use factory function returning fresh defaults.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Shared mutable DEFAULTS object. Missing = {} on destructure-only parameter. Too many required keys without validation error messages. Mixing positional and options in same function.

blocks.text: Version options: accept unknown keys silently vs strict — document **strictOptions** flag for SDKs. **Required<Pick<T,'url'>> & Partial<T>** pattern in TS. Deprecate positional overloads with wrapper that maps to options object. Log unknown keys in dev to catch typos (`timeOut` vs `timeout`).

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Function f({ a = 1 }) without = {} and cannot explain f() behavior. Unaware shared DEFAULTS mutation bug. Cannot compare to C# optional/named parameters.

interviewTakeaways: Options object replaces long positional parameter lists.
Always use = {} on destructure-only param if call with zero args is valid.
60s: Named params via object keys. Destructure defaults. C# named optional args similar ergonomics. Validate required. Avoid shared mutable DEFAULTS.
Follow-up: design fetch wrapper options with timeout, retries, and signal.
commonPitfalls: Missing = {} causing TypeError on f() with no arguments.
Mutable nested objects in shared DEFAULTS.
Strong answer: merge pattern, validation, TS Partial, C# named args comparison.
